title_en: Fujian Sanmu Group Co., Ltd. v. Fujian Province Quanzhou Huangxing Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over a pre-sale contract for commercial housing
ruling_gist_en: According to Articles 2, 10, and 34 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, a party bears the burden of proof to produce evidence supporting the facts on which its claim is based or refuting the facts on which the opposing party's claim is based. When a party submits documentary evidence to the people's court, it shall produce the original and fulfill its burden of proof actively, comprehensively, and correctly within the time limit for举证 designated by the people's court. Therefore, if one party to a contract claims that the original copy of the contract text provided by the opposing party to the court is not authentic, it shall submit to the court the original copy of the contract text in its possession and other relevant evidence. If it cannot submit the original copy of the contract text to the court, nor can it provide other evidence of sufficient probative value to disprove the authenticity of the original copy of the contract text provided by the opposing party, the people's court shall, based on the principle of preponderance of evidence, determine that the original copy of the contract text provided by the opposing party is authentic.

full_text_en:
Fujian Sanmu Group Co., Ltd. v. Fujian Quanzhou Huangxing Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over commercial housing pre-sale contract

Ruling Summary

Pursuant to Articles 2, 10, and 34 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, a party has the burden to produce evidence to prove the facts on which its claims are based or to rebut the facts on which the opposing party's claims are based. A party that provides documentary evidence to the People's Court shall provide the original document and shall actively, comprehensively, and correctly complete its burden of proof within the time limit for producing evidence designated by the People's Court. Therefore, where one party to a contract claims that the original contract document provided by the other party to the court is not authentic, it shall provide to the court the original contract document in its own possession and other relevant evidence; if it cannot provide the original contract document and also cannot provide other evidence with conclusive probative force to disprove the authenticity of the original contract document provided by the other party, the People's Court shall, based on the preponderance of evidence principle, determine that the original contract document provided by the other party is authentic.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

No. 104, Final Civil Judgment of the First Circuit (2004)

Appellant (original plaintiff): Fujian Sanmu Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 162, Junzhu Road, Fuzhou Development Zone, Fujian Province.

Legal representative: Lan Jun, Chairperson of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Zheng Decheng, lawyer of Fujian Chuangxing Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Shen Ming, lawyer of Beijing Fusheng Law Firm.

Respondent (original defendant): Fujian Quanzhou Huangxing Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 518, Huangxing Building, Middle Section of Fengze Street, Fengze District, Quanzhou, Fujian Province.

Legal representative: Lin Junqing, Chairperson of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Liu Shouming, lawyer of Beijing Tianning Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wei Zheng, lawyer of Fujian Zhili Law Firm.

The appellant, Fujian Sanmu Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Sanmu Company), appeals to this Court against the civil judgment [2003] Min Min Chu Zi No. 3 rendered by the Fujian High People's Court in the case of dispute over commercial housing pre-sale contract with the respondent, Fujian Quanzhou Huangxing Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huangxing Company). This Court formed a collegial panel according to law and held a hearing of this case on December 14, 2004. The agents ad litem of Sanmu Company, Zheng Decheng and Shen Ming, and the agents ad litem of Huangxing Company, Liu Shouming and Wei Zheng, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

The court of first instance found the following facts:

On May 26, 2000, Huangxing Company, upon approval, contributed the main building floors 1 to 21, shopping mall floors 3 to 4, and 80 parking spaces on basement level 1 of the Huangxing Building it was developing as capital contribution to establish Fujian Nannan Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Nannan Company).

On June 1, 2000, Nannan Company, Sanmu Company, and Fuzhou Shenda Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shenda Company) entered into an Agreement stipulating: This Agreement is the overall framework agreement for the asset restructuring among the three parties. In case of conflict between any agreement signed for the performance of this Agreement and this Agreement, this Agreement shall prevail. Nannan Company would participate as a shareholder in Sanmu Company by means of asset restructuring such as equity transfer, with cash of RMB 30 million and real estate valued at RMB 134.87 million. Sanmu Company would purchase real estate of Huangxing Building developed by Huangxing Company valued at RMB 134.87 million through methods such as cooperative investment. The floors and area of the purchased property would be separately specified in a building sale contract and executed according to the terms of that contract. Nannan Company guaranteed that the full amount of the real estate transfer payment received by Huangxing Company must be used to purchase the shares of Sanmu Company held by Zhuocheng Company, Gaode Company, and Huatian Company. After Nannan Company, through its affiliated entities or natural persons, acquired Zhuocheng Company, Gaode Company, and Huatian Company, it would enjoy all rights and obligations of a shareholder granted by the Company Law and the company's articles of association.

On June 15, 2000, Sanmu Company and Huangxing Company entered into a Part of Huangxing Building Property Underwriting Agreement (hereinafter referred to as the Underwriting Agreement), stipulating that Sanmu Company would underwrite 1,132.67 square meters of property on the shopping mall floor of the main building of Huangxing Building developed by Huangxing Company, 70 parking spaces on basement level 1, and 70 parking spaces on basement level 2, at an underwriting price of RMB 51 million. On June 26 of the same year, Huangxing Company sent a letter to Sanmu Company, requesting that RMB 50 million of the underwriting payment be paid to Fujian Shunfeng Yinzhou Business Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shunfeng Company) and RMB 1 million be paid to Fujian Provincial Overseas Talents Exchange Center (hereinafter referred to as the Talents Exchange Center). Accordingly, on June 30 of the same year, Sanmu Company paid RMB 51 million.

On June 12, 2000, Sanmu Company and Quanzhou World Trade Commerce and Business Planning Promotional Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as World Trade Commerce Company) entered into an Agreement on Cooperative Investment in Entertainment City and High-End Club (hereinafter referred to as the Entertainment City and Club Agreement), stipulating that Sanmu Company would invest RMB 35.87 million to cooperatively invest with World Trade Commerce Company in the Entertainment City and High-End Club of Quanzhou Huangxing Building. On August 23 of the same year, Sanmu Company, World Trade Commerce Company, and Huangxing Company entered into a Supplemental Agreement stipulating that Sanmu Company would use its already invested RMB 35.87 million to purchase from World Trade Commerce Company approximately 4,000 square meters of property on the third floor of Huangxing Building over which World Trade Commerce Company had the right of disposal. The floors, area, price, and related matters of the purchased property would be governed by a separate building sale contract to be signed between Sanmu Company and Huangxing Company.

On June 20, 2000, Sanmu Company and Quanzhou World Trade Center Hotel Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as World Trade Hotel Company) entered into an Agreement on Cooperative Investment in Quanzhou World Trade Center Hotel (hereinafter referred to as the Hotel Agreement), stipulating that Sanmu Company would invest RMB 48 million in Quanzhou World Trade Center Hotel. On August 23 of the same year, Sanmu Company, World Trade Hotel Company, and Huangxing Company entered into a Supplemental Agreement stipulating that Sanmu Company would use its already invested RMB 48 million to purchase from World Trade Hotel Company the property on the second floor and floors 5 to 21 of Huangxing Building over which World Trade Hotel Company had the right of disposal. The floors, area, price, and related matters of the purchased property would be governed by a separate building sale contract to be signed between Sanmu Company and Huangxing Company.

On June 26, 2000, World Trade Commerce Company sent a letter to Sanmu Company, requesting that the investment amount of RMB 35.87 million be paid to the Talents Exchange Center. On June 28 of the same year, World Trade Hotel Company sent a letter to Sanmu Company, requesting that the investment amount of RMB 48 million be paid to Fujian Provincial Straits High-Tech Transformation Center (hereinafter referred to as the Technology Transformation Center). Accordingly, on June 30 of the same year, Sanmu Company paid RMB 35.87 million and RMB 48 million to the Talents Exchange Center and the Technology Transformation Center, respectively.

Thereafter, Li Jianna and Chen Jian, shareholders of Zhuocheng Company, transferred all their shares in Sanmu Company to Qiu Guolong and Wang Jinxing, a shareholder of Nannan Company; Fang Jinhua and Guo Jian, shareholders of Gaode Company, transferred all their shares in Sanmu Company to Wang Jinxing and Yang Lizhen, shareholders of Nannan Company; Zhou Xunnan and Zhang Datian, shareholders of Huatian Company, transferred all their shares in Sanmu Company to Wang Liyu and Yang Lizhen, shareholders of Nannan Company. Shunfeng Company, the Talents Exchange Center, and the Technology Transformation Center respectively transferred the payments received from Sanmu Company to Li Jianna and others.

On June 10, 2002, Sanmu Company and Fuzhou Tianyi Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tianyi Company) entered into a Contract Rights Transfer Agreement stipulating: Sanmu Company would transfer to Tianyi Company all its contract rights, including the property underwriting and disposal rights under the Underwriting Agreement, for RMB 51 million. After Tianyi Company paid the transfer price, it would enjoy all of Sanmu Company's rights under the Underwriting Agreement. On June 13 of the same year, Tianyi Company paid RMB 51 million to Sanmu Company. On June 14 of the same year, Sanmu Company issued a Notice of Transfer of Contract Rights under the "Huangxing Building Part Property Underwriting Agreement" to Huangxing Company, stating that it had transferred all rights and interests under the Underwriting Agreement to Tianyi Company and requesting Huangxing Company to perform its obligation to deliver the property to Tianyi Company.

On June 11, 2002, Sanmu Company and Fuzhou Longyi Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Longyi Company) entered into a Contract Rights Transfer Agreement stipulating: Sanmu Company would transfer to Longyi Company all its contract rights, including the property disposal rights under the two cooperative investment agreements and two supplemental agreements it had respectively signed with World Trade Commerce Company, World Trade Hotel Company, and Huangxing Company, for a total of RMB 83.87 million. After Longyi Company paid the first installment of RMB 65 million, it would enjoy all of Sanmu Company's rights and interests under the two cooperative investment agreements and two supplemental agreements. On June 14 of the same year, Longyi Company paid RMB 65 million to Sanmu Company.

On the same day, Sanmu Company respectively issued notices of transfer of contract rights to World Trade Commerce Company, World Trade Hotel Company, and Huangxing Company, stating that it had transferred all rights and interests under the two cooperative investment agreements and two supplemental agreements to Longyi Company and requesting World Trade Commerce Company, World Trade Hotel Company, and Huangxing Company to perform their obligation to deliver the property to Longyi Company.

After the signing of the above-mentioned Underwriting Agreement, Entertainment City and Club Agreement and its Supplemental Agreement, Hotel Agreement and its Supplemental Agreement, Sanmu Company and Huangxing Company signed three Commercial Housing Purchase Contracts (hereinafter referred to as the Housing Contracts), which replaced the Underwriting Agreement, the Entertainment City and Club Agreement and its Supplemental Agreement, and the Hotel Agreement and its Supplemental Agreement, and became the final agreements establishing the commercial housing purchase and sale relationship between Sanmu Company and Huangxing Company.

The above facts have been found and determined in the effective civil judgments [2002] Min Min Chu Zi No. 4 and No. 5 (hereinafter referred to as the [2002] Min Min Chu Zi No. 4 and No. 5 civil judgments) of the Fujian High People's Court.

On June 20, 2003, Sanmu Company filed a lawsuit alleging: After Sanmu Company paid RMB 134.87 million in accordance with the Agreement and other related agreements, it discovered that Huangxing Company had already contributed the properties under the three Housing Contracts as capital to Nannan Company in April 2000. Huangxing Company unilaterally filled in the content on blank Housing Contracts that Sanmu Company had already signed for the purpose of applying for housing pre-sale registration, transferring to Sanmu Company floors 8, 9, and 10 of the main building and parking spaces 31 to 44 for RMB 51 million, floors 5, 6, and 7 of the main building for RMB 48 million, and floors 11 and 12 of the main building and parking spaces 45 to 62 for RMB 35.87 million. The pre-sale property price was RMB 14,126 per square meter, and each parking space was RMB 215,000, both higher than the normal market price of the local real estate market, showing obvious unfairness. Huangxing Company concealed the fact that the transferred properties were contributed as shares, causing Sanmu Company to enter into the agreements without knowing the truth. According to the [2002] Min Min Chu Zi No. 4 and No. 5 civil judgments, the contract rights acquired by Tianyi Company and Longyi Company did not exist, and the content of the three Housing Contracts was not the true intention of Sanmu Company. Therefore, Sanmu Company requested the rescission of the three Housing Contracts and an order for Huangxing Company to return the purchase price of RMB 134.87 million and interest.

Huangxing Company argued in its defense: Sanmu Company's claims are no different from those in the [2002] Min Min Chu Zi No. 4 and No. 5 civil judgments. The Agreement stipulated that "the properties of Huangxing Building that Sanmu Company intends to purchase are under construction and have been contributed as capital to Nannan Company's registered capital." Huangxing Company did not conceal or defraud. The three Housing Contracts have been found to be authentic and lawful by the [2002] Min Min Chu Zi No. 4 and No. 5 civil judgments. Huangxing Company used properties to exchange for the legal person shares of Sanmu Company held by Zhuocheng Company, Gaode Company, and Huatian Company. Sanmu Company did not actually pay the purchase price, and its request for a refund and claim of obvious unfairness regarding the price is unfounded. Therefore, Huangxing Company requested the dismissal of Sanmu Company's complaint or the rejection of its claims.

The court of first instance also found the following:

In the three Housing Contracts signed between Sanmu Company and Huangxing Company (hereinafter respectively referred to as Housing Contract 1, Housing Contract 2, and Housing Contract 3), Party A affixed the company seal of Huangxing Company and the personal seal of Yang Lizhen (Chairperson), and Party B affixed the company seal of Sanmu Company and the signature of Chen Weihui (President), but none of them indicated the date of signing. The three Housing Contracts stipulated: Sanmu Company purchased commercial housing located in the middle section of Fengze Street, Quanzhou, in Huangxing Building. Housing Contract 1 stipulated: Main building floors 5, 6, and 7, 1,132.67 square meters per floor, total area 3,398 square meters, unit price RMB 14,126 per square meter, total amount RMB 48 million. Housing Contract 2 stipulated: Main building floors 8, 9, and 10, 1,132.67 square meters per floor, total area 3,398 square meters, unit price RMB 14,126 per square meter, total amount RMB 48 million, underground parking spaces 31 to 44, unit price RMB 214,286, total amount RMB 3 million, aggregate total amount RMB 51 million. Housing Contract 3 stipulated: Main building floors 11 and 12, 1,132.67 square meters per floor, total area 2,265.34 square meters, unit price RMB 14,126 per square meter, total amount RMB 32 million, underground parking spaces 45 to 62, unit price RMB 215,000, total amount RMB 3.87 million, aggregate total amount RMB 35.87 million. The three Housing Contracts specially stipulated: The total area above refers to the construction area (including shared common area). If there is any discrepancy between the measured and registered area and the area agreed in this contract, this contract shall not be rescinded, and the parties shall not compensate each other. Sanmu Company chose to pay the full amount in a lump sum, with the entire purchase price paid in full upon the signing of the contract. The purchase price stipulated in Housing Contract 1 was RMB 48 million, in Housing Contract 2 was RMB 51 million, and in Housing Contract 3 was RMB 35.87 million. Huangxing Company shall deliver the property to Sanmu Company before December 30, 2003. This contract shall take effect on the date of signing by both parties, etc.

In the trials of the [2002] Min Min Chu Zi No. 4 and No. 5 cases in the Fujian High People's Court, the China Criminal Police University (hereinafter referred to as the Criminal Police University), commissioned by the court, conducted a forensic examination on the authenticity of the three Housing Contracts and concluded: As to the time of filling in the content concerning the sale price, area, delivery time, etc., in the three Housing Contracts and the relative writing time between the filled-in content and the signature of the agent of Party B Sanmu Company on page 6, it is currently not possible to make a determination. The [2002] Min Min Chu Zi No. 4 and No. 5 civil judgments found the three Housing Contracts to be authentic and determined that Housing Contract 2 was formed after June 15, 2000, and Housing Contract 1 and Housing Contract 3 were formed after August 23 of the same year.

During the first-instance proceedings of this case, Sanmu Company admitted the authenticity of the company seal and signature on the three Housing Contracts but claimed that the other content was unilaterally filled in by Huangxing Company. Sanmu Company applied for a forensic examination of the seal impression and handwriting time on the three Housing Contracts but could not provide any forensic institution with the relevant technical capability.

The court of first instance also found the following:

In the trials of the [2002] Min Min Chu Zi No. 4 and No. 5 cases, Tianyi Company, Longyi Company, and Huangxing Company acknowledged the fact that on June 1, 2000, Nannan Company, Sanmu Company, and Shenda Company signed the Agreement. However, Tianyi Company and Longyi Company contended that there were differences in content between the original of the Agreement provided by Huangxing Company and the copy of the Agreement they had submitted regarding pages 1 to 2. The Criminal Police University, commissioned by the court, issued an Expert Opinion on the Agreement provided by Huangxing Company, the content being: 1. Upon examination, the three pages of text of the Agreement were all printed on A4 paper in No. 4 Song font, with no difference in line spacing. However, further examination revealed that the bottom edge of pages 1 and 2 measured approximately 209.5 mm, while the bottom edge of page 3 measured approximately 210 mm. Compared with page 3, the text block on pages 1 and 2 was shifted to the upper left, and the page number was shifted to the upper right. On pages 1 and 2, besides the text ink, there were numerous toner defects of the same distribution and shape, while no such defects were found on page 3. The strokes on pages 1 and 2 were slightly thicker than those on page 3. The toner ink on pages 1 and 2 was non-magnetic, while the toner ink on page 3 was magnetic. The above differences reflect the characteristics of documents printed at different times and by different printing machines. The conclusion was: Pages 1 and 2 of the Agreement were printed separately from page 3 by different printing machines. Based on this, the [2002] Min Min Chu Zi No. 4 and No. 5 civil judgments determined that the Agreement provided by Huangxing Company was an original, and since Sanmu Company and Shenda Company could not provide the original, and based solely on the statements of Tianyi Company and Longyi Company, it could not be determined that Huangxing Company had altered the Agreement. However, according to the expert opinion, the process of forming the Agreement was unclear, and it could not be used as the sole basis for deciding the case.

During the first-instance proceedings of this case, Sanmu Company acknowledged the fact that it had signed the Agreement with Shenda Company and Nannan Company, but claimed that the tripartite Agreement did not contain the content that "the Huangxing Building has already been contributed as capital to Nannan Company's registered capital," and that pages 1 and 2 of the Agreement submitted by Huangxing Company had been altered. To this end, Sanmu Company provided a copy of the Agreement (the same copy provided by Tianyi Company and Longyi Company in the [2002] Min Min Chu Zi No. 4 and No. 5 cases), in which the content of Article 5 on page 2 was: Since the properties of Huangxing Building purchased by Sanmu Company are under construction, upon the completion of the construction and acceptance inspection of such properties and satisfaction of all conditions required for obtaining the title certificate, Nannan Company must notify Sanmu Company to go through the title registration procedures. Within ten days after Nannan Company notifies Sanmu Company to go through the procedures, Sanmu Company shall be responsible for releasing the shares of Sanmu Group held by Gaode Company, Zhuocheng Company, and Huatian Company, being 8.1 million shares, 7.8 million shares, and 6,232,587 shares, respectively. Article 6 stated: Before notifying Sanmu Company to go through the procedures, Nannan Company must ensure that the rate of return on the cooperative investment project between Sanmu Company and Nannan Company is not lower than Sanmu Company's net asset return rate for the same period. Sanmu Company also provided evidence including two Guarantee Letters from Gaode Company and Huatian Company respectively to Sanmu Company dated October 12, 2000, and a Statement on the Tripartite Agreement among Shenda Company, Nannan Company, and Sanmu Company (hereinafter referred to as the Statement) issued by Shenda Company on September 25, 2002.

The court of first instance also found the following: The Huangxing Building was developed by Huangxing Company. It obtained the State-owned Land Use Certificate in February 1998, the Construction Project Planning Permit in October 1999, and the Commercial Housing Pre-Sale Permit in December 1999, and was authorized to pre-sell a total area of 36,039 square meters of commercial, residential, and office space in the Huangxing Building, comprising 200 units.

During the proceedings in the court of first instance, Sanmu Company argued that the properties approved for pre-sale by Huangxing Company did not include the basement parking spaces and the 5th to 12th floors of the main building under the three Commercial Housing Contracts, and that more than 16,000 square meters were used by Huangxing Company itself. The evidence provided by Sanmu Company included: (1) Huangxing Company's Application Form for Pre-sale of Commercial Housing dated November 22, 1999, in which the project name under the overview of properties for pre-sale was filled in as "Huangxing Tower Podium," with a total land area of 6,040 square meters, total building area of 20,221 square meters, residential area of 12,000 square meters, and 65 units; on December 2 of the same year, the Quanzhou Municipal Construction Commission stamped and signed in the column for industry authority approval opinion, stating, "Approved for the issuance of the pre-sale permit for Huangxing Tower, with a pre-sale area of 36,039 square meters, totaling 200 commercial and residential units (the original pre-sale permit No. 001 for 98 houses approved 24,039 square meters is hereby revoked and void)"; (2) the Certificate issued by the Quanzhou Municipal Real Estate Administration Bureau on September 10, 2003, which stated, "The pre-sale permit No. 052 (99) issued to Huangxing Company approves a pre-sale area of 36,039 square meters (including 3,360 square meters of shops and 32,679 square meters of residential units), and does not include the basement levels 1 and 2"; (3) the House Ownership Certificate No. 28242 issued to Huangxing Company by the Quanzhou Municipal Real Estate Administration Bureau on July 4, 2003, which stated, "Owner: Huangxing Company; Location: Huangxing Tower, Middle Section of Fengze Street, Fengze District; Property type: joint-stock enterprise property; Building has 23 floors; Building area: 46,425.17 + 6,104.51 square meters; Land certificate No. 200021 (98); Usable area: 5,550.3 square meters; Remarks column: Commercial housing sold; pre-sale area of 36,039 square meters; other area for own use"; (4) the Huangxing Tower Project Proposal Report submitted by Huangxing Company to the Quanzhou Municipal Development and Reform Commission, the Project Proposal Approval approving Huangxing Company to build 18,000 square meters of commercial housing and 16,000 square meters of self-use housing, the Construction Permit for Huangxing Tower, and the Certificate of Completion and Acceptance for Construction Project Filing, all with building area filled in as 47,142.6 square meters; and (5) the On-site Survey Form for House and Land Location Map prepared by the Quanzhou Municipal Real Estate Surveying Team, containing the total building area of Huangxing Tower and the building area of each floor, and floor plans of floors 1 to 21 of Huangxing Tower.

The court of first instance further found: The civil judgments in [2002] Min Min Chu Zi No. 4 and No. 5 determined that: (1) On June 15, 2000, Sanmu Company and Huangxing Company signed the Exclusive Sales Agreement; on June 26, 2000, Huangxing Company sent a letter to Sanmu Company, requesting that out of the exclusive sales payment of RMB 51 million under the agreement, RMB 50 million be paid to Shunfeng Company and RMB 1 million be paid to the Talent Exchange Center. Accordingly, Sanmu Company paid RMB 51 million on June 30, 2000. (2) On June 12, 2000, Sanmu Company and World Trade Business Company signed the Entertainment City and Club Agreement; on June 26 of the same year, World Trade Business Company sent a letter to Sanmu Company, requesting that the amount of RMB 35.87 million under the agreement be paid to the Talent Exchange Center. Accordingly, Sanmu Company paid RMB 35.87 million to the Talent Exchange Center on June 30 of the same year. (3) On June 20, 2000, Sanmu Company and World Trade Hotel Company signed the Hotel Agreement; on June 28 of the same year, World Trade Hotel Company sent a letter to Sanmu Company, requesting that the amount of RMB 48 million under the agreement be paid to the Technology Transfer Center. Accordingly, Sanmu Company paid RMB 48 million to the Technology Transfer Center on June 30 of the same year.

During the proceedings in the first instance, Sanmu Company argued, based on the findings of the effective judgments, that it had paid the total purchase price of RMB 134.87 million for the three Commercial Housing Contracts. It further argued that, according to the content of the Agreement confirmed by the civil judgments in [2002] Min Min Chu Zi No. 4 and No. 5, paragraph 4 provided: "In this asset restructuring, Sanmu Company purchases through cooperative investment and other means from Huangxing Company the properties of Huangxing Tower developed by Huangxing Company with a value of RMB 134.87 million. The floors and areas of the purchased properties shall be separately stipulated in a housing sale contract, to be performed in accordance with the terms of the housing sale contract." Accordingly, the RMB 134.87 million consisted of the three amounts determined by the effective judgments, of which RMB 51 million had been received by Huangxing Company. As for the amounts of RMB 48 million and RMB 35.87 million, according to paragraph 4 of the Supplemental Agreements signed on August 28, 2000 by Sanmu Company, Huangxing Company, World Trade Hotel Company, and World Trade Business Company, which stated: "Sanmu Company agrees to use the invested funds of RMB 48 million and RMB 35.87 million to respectively purchase from World Trade Hotel Company and World Trade Business Company certain properties in the main building of Huangxing Tower over which they have the right of disposal. The floors, areas, prices, and related matters of the purchased properties shall be governed by the housing sale contract to be separately signed between Sanmu Company and Huangxing Company." This proved that the three parties to the Supplemental Agreements had reached an agreement to convert the two amounts of RMB 48 million and RMB 35.87 million invested by Sanmu Company into the purchase price of the properties.

The court of first instance made the following findings based on the issues in dispute between the parties:

I. Whether Sanmu Company's claim constituted a repeated lawsuit. The court of first instance held: The lawsuit filed by Sanmu Company sought to rescind the three Commercial Housing Contracts signed between Sanmu Company and Huangxing Company. The subject of the lawsuit and the legal relationship were different from those in the cases [2002] Min Min Chu Zi No. 4 and No. 5, and thus there was no repeated lawsuit.

II. Whether the three Commercial Housing Contracts that Sanmu Company sought to rescind were genuine. The court of first instance held: The authenticity and the time of signing of the three Commercial Housing Contracts between Huangxing Company and Sanmu Company had been confirmed by the effective civil judgments in [2002] Min Min Chu Zi No. 4 and No. 5. In those two cases, the time of filling in the contents of the three Commercial Housing Contracts regarding sales price, area, delivery time, and the relative writing time of the signature of the agent of Sanmu Company on page 6 had been examined by the Criminal Police College, which concluded that "no appraisal can currently be made." In the present case, Sanmu Company applied for an appraisal of the time of the seals and handwriting on the three Commercial Housing Contracts. Since both parties did not dispute the authenticity of the signatures and seals, it can be determined that both parties acknowledged the contents of the contracts. Even if Sanmu Company claimed that its seal and signature were affixed first and Huangxing Company filled in the contents unilaterally afterward, the consequences should be borne by Sanmu Company itself, because such a situation was foreseeable by Sanmu Company. Therefore, a new appraisal was unnecessary. Moreover, Sanmu Company failed to provide the identification of an appraisal unit with the relevant expertise, and failed to provide evidence sufficient to overturn the findings of the civil judgments in [2002] Min Min Chu Zi No. 4 and No. 5 regarding the authenticity of the three Commercial Housing Contracts. Its claim that the three Commercial Housing Contracts were blank contracts signed and sealed by Sanmu Company and then unilaterally filled in by Huangxing Company could not be established due to insufficient evidence.

III. Whether, at the time of signing the Commercial Housing Contracts, Sanmu Company knew that Huangxing Company had invested the properties under the contracts as capital contributions into Nannan Company. The court of first instance held: (1) Sanmu Company, Nannan Company, and Shenda Company signed the Agreement, stipulating that Sanmu Company would provide RMB 134.87 million for Nannan Company to acquire the legal person shares of Sanmu Company held by Huatian Company, Zhuocheng Company, and Gaode Company, and then these three companies would transfer the legal person shares of Sanmu Company to a subsidiary of Nannan Company; Nannan Company would transfer to Sanmu Company the properties of Huangxing Tower developed by Huangxing Company as consideration. To this end, the parties successively signed the Exclusive Sales Agreement, the Entertainment City and Club Agreement and its Supplemental Agreement, the Hotel Agreement and its Supplemental Agreement, and finally Sanmu Company and Huangxing Company signed the three Commercial Housing Contracts. (2) Before the three parties signed the Agreement, Huangxing Company had already contributed, as capital, the properties including those under the three Commercial Housing Contracts, specifically floors 1 to 21 of the main building of Huangxing Tower, floors 3 to 4 of the shopping mall, and 80 parking spaces on basement level 1, to establish Nannan Company. (3) The copy of the Agreement provided by Sanmu Company, which did not contain the clause "the properties of Huangxing Tower purchased by Sanmu Company are construction in progress and have been invested as capital into Nannan Company," could not alone serve as evidence to determine the content of the tripartite Agreement. The Explanation issued by Shenda Company provided by Sanmu Company constituted witness testimony. Since Shenda Company did not appear in court to testify, it could not be used alone as evidence to determine the facts of the case. Moreover, Shenda Company, as a signatory to the tripartite Agreement, did not produce the original of the Agreement to verify the Explanation it issued. Therefore, the Explanation of Shenda Company could not serve as a basis to confirm the content of the tripartite Agreement provided by Sanmu Company, nor could it prove that Huangxing Company had altered pages 1 and 2 of the Agreement. The two Letters of Guarantee from Gaode Company and Huatian Company provided by Sanmu Company bore the seals of the two companies, and their authenticity could be confirmed. Huangxing Company's claim that they were false was unsubstantiated and not accepted. Although the content of these two Letters of Guarantee referred to Article 6 of the tripartite Agreement provided by Sanmu Company, Article 6 of the tripartite Agreement provided by Sanmu Company did not contain any stipulation that Nannan Company should provide a guarantee, and Sanmu Company failed to further prove that Nannan Company knew about and approved of Gaode Company and Huatian Company acting as guarantors for its performance of the tripartite Agreement. Therefore, the two Letters of Guarantee were insufficient to corroborate the authenticity of the tripartite Agreement provided by Sanmu Company. The appraisal conclusion of the Criminal Police College regarding the tripartite Agreement provided by Huangxing Company only showed that the printing process of the Agreement was unclear, and could not prove that the first two pages of the Agreement provided by Huangxing Company had been altered. The effective civil judgments in [2002] Min Min Chu Zi No. 4 and No. 5 did not determine that the copies submitted by Tianyi Company and Longyi Company were authentic, nor did they determine that the first two pages of the Agreement provided by Huangxing Company had been altered.

In summary, the four pieces of evidence provided by Sanmu Company could not corroborate the authenticity of the tripartite Agreement submitted by Sanmu Company. The Agreement provided by Huangxing Company was an original. The appraisal conclusion of the Criminal Police College only indicated that the printing process of the Agreement was unclear, which was insufficient to deny the authenticity and the legality of the source of the Agreement.

Given that both parties acknowledged the existence of the tripartite Agreement among Sanmu Company, Nannan Company, and Shenda Company, and that Sanmu Company failed to submit the original of the Agreement, the original of the Agreement provided by Huangxing Company was admissible as evidence, proving that Article 5 of the tripartite Agreement contained the clause "the properties of Huangxing Tower purchased by Sanmu Company are construction in progress and have been invested as capital into Nannan Company." Sanmu Company's failure to provide the original of the tripartite Agreement meant that it must bear the consequences of failure to provide evidence.

IV. Whether the relevant approvals for the construction and sale of Huangxing Tower could prove that the properties under the three Commercial Housing Contracts had been approved for pre-sale. The court of first instance held: (1) The State-owned Land Use Certificate, the Construction Project Planning Permit, and the Commercial Housing Pre-sale Permit obtained by Huangxing Company could prove that Huangxing Tower was approved for construction and obtained approval for pre-sale of 36,039 square meters in December 1999. (2) Neither the Commercial Housing Pre-sale Permit, the Application Form for Pre-sale of Commercial Housing, nor the Certificate from the Quanzhou Municipal Real Estate Administration Bureau could prove whether the properties under the three Commercial Housing Contracts were approved for pre-sale; the Huangxing Tower Project Proposal Report, the Project Proposal Approval, the Construction Permit, the Certificate of Completion and Acceptance for Construction Project Filing, and the On-site Survey Form for House and Land Location Map also could not further corroborate that the properties under the three Commercial Housing Contracts were not within the scope of the pre-sale approval obtained by Huangxing Company. (3) Huangxing Company obtained the State-owned Land Use Certificate for the construction land of Huangxing Tower on February 26, 1998, and obtained the House Ownership Certificate for Huangxing Tower (including the properties under the three Commercial Housing Contracts) on July 4, 2003.

V. Whether the three Commercial Housing Contracts had been actually performed. The court of first instance held: The signing of the three Commercial Housing Contracts in dispute between Sanmu Company and Huangxing Company was the performance of the tripartite Agreement. The effective civil judgments in [2002] Min Min Chu Zi No. 4 and No. 5 had determined that Sanmu Company performed the Exclusive Sales Agreement, the Entertainment City and Club Agreement, and the Hotel Agreement, and successively paid RMB 134.87 million in accordance with the contracts and the requirements of the other parties. The contents of the telegrams from Fang Jinhua, Zhou Xunnan, and Zhang Datian could not prove that Sanmu Company had not actually made the payments.

The three Commercial Housing Contracts in dispute were signed and sealed by Sanmu Company and Huangxing Company. Sanmu Company's claim that Huangxing Company unilaterally filled in the contents of the blank contracts that Sanmu Company had already signed and sealed could not be established due to insufficient evidence. The content of these three Commercial Housing Contracts reflected a pre-sale commercial housing contractual relationship between the parties. Although there was insufficient evidence to prove that the properties under the contracts in Huangxing Tower had been approved for pre-sale, at the time Sanmu Company filed the lawsuit and before the contractual delivery date, Huangxing Tower had already been constructed, and Huangxing Company had obtained the State-owned Land Use Certificate and the House Ownership Certificate for Huangxing Tower, thereby meeting the conditions for the transfer of the properties under the contracts. Therefore, the three Commercial Housing Contracts were lawful and valid.

Since the three Commercial Housing Contracts were signed by Sanmu Company and Huangxing Company to perform the tripartite Agreement dated June 1, 2000 among Nannan Company, Sanmu Company, and Shenda Company, which provided that "Sanmu Company shall fund Nannan Company to acquire the legal person shares of Sanmu Company held by Zhuocheng Company, Gaode Company, and Huatian Company, and Nannan Company shall transfer to Sanmu Company the properties of Huangxing Tower developed by Huangxing Company as consideration," the intentions of both parties were clear. There was no situation of one party taking advantage of the other's superior position or the other party's haste or inexperience, and the agreement that the contract price was higher than the market price did not exceed the scope permitted by law. Therefore, Sanmu Company's claim of obvious unfairness on the ground that the contract price was significantly higher than the market price lacked legal basis. Article 5 of the tripartite Agreement provided by Huangxing Company could prove that at the time of signing the tripartite Agreement, Sanmu Company already knew or should have known that Huangxing Company had contributed the Huangxing Tower properties as capital into Nannan Company, while Sanmu Company's claim that Huangxing Company concealed this fact could not be established due to insufficient evidence. Therefore, Sanmu Company's request to rescind the three Commercial Housing Contracts on the ground that Huangxing Company's concealment of facts constituted fraud lacked factual basis and did not comply with Article 54 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and was not supported. In accordance with Article 64, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 54, paragraphs 1 and 2 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 2 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, the court of first instance rendered the following judgment: Sanmu Company's claims are dismissed. Case acceptance fee of RMB 793,882.86 and property preservation fee of RMB 783,873 shall be borne by Sanmu Company.

Sanmu Company, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to this Court, requesting that the three Commercial Housing Contracts be rescinded, that Huangxing Company be ordered to return the purchase price of RMB 134.87 million plus corresponding interest, and that Huangxing Company bear all litigation costs in this case. The facts and reasons were as follows:

1. The judgment of first instance held that the appraisal conclusion of the Criminal Police College that the printing process of the Agreement was unclear was insufficient to deny the authenticity and lawful source of the Agreement, yet it recognized the validity of the Agreement. This contradicted the determination in the civil judgments [2002] Min Min Chu Zi No. 4 and No. 5 that it could not be used alone as a basis for deciding the case. The Explanation issued by Shenda Company and the Letters of Guarantee issued by Gaode Company and Huatian Company mutually corroborated that the copy of the Agreement provided by Sanmu Company was consistent with the original. The judgment of first instance recognized the authenticity of the Letters of Guarantee of Gaode Company and Huatian Company, but then determined that the Letters of Guarantee were insufficient to corroborate the authenticity of the Agreement submitted by Sanmu Company. This was erroneous. The properties under the three Commercial Housing Contracts included the main building and underground parking spaces. However, the Commercial Housing Pre-sale Permit, the Application Form for Pre-sale of Commercial Housing, the House Ownership Certificate for Huangxing Tower, and the Certificate from the Quanzhou Municipal Real Estate Administration Bureau all proved that the main building and underground parking spaces under the three Commercial Housing Contracts were not within the pre-sale scope. When negotiating the purchase and sale of the properties under the Commercial Housing Contracts, Huangxing Company concealed the true situation of the properties and the lack of pre-sale qualification, causing Sanmu Company to make a mistaken expression of intent, which constituted fraud. The judgment of first instance erred by not recognizing Sanmu Company's claim that Huangxing Company unilaterally filled in the blank contracts on the ground that Sanmu Company failed to provide an appraisal unit.

2. The price per square meter under the three Commercial Housing Contracts was RMB 14,126, and each parking space was RMB 215,000. According to the Asset Appraisal Report issued by Fujian Huaxing Certified Public Accountants, when Huangxing Company invested Huangxing Tower into Nannan Company, it appraised floors 1 to 21 of the main building, floors 3 to 4 of the shopping mall, and 80 parking spaces on basement level 1 at approximately RMB 150 million. The properties under the Commercial Housing Contracts in this case only comprised 8 floors of the main building and 30 parking spaces, with an area less than one-third of the entire building, yet the price was as high as over RMB 130 million, which was obviously unfair. The judgment of first instance erred in applying the law by holding that the agreed contract price, which was higher than the market price, did not exceed the scope permitted by law.

3. During the proceedings in the first instance, Sanmu Company applied for an investigation into the scope of the properties under the Commercial Housing Pre-sale Permit obtained by Huangxing Company. However, the court of first instance did not notify Sanmu Company whether it approved the application, nor did it inform Sanmu Company of the results of the investigation, thus violating legal procedures.

Huangxing Company responded: The judgment of first instance was clear in finding the facts and correct in applying the law. It requested that Sanmu Company's appeal be dismissed and the original judgment be affirmed. The facts and reasons were: The tripartite Agreement stipulated that the properties of Huangxing Tower purchased by Sanmu Company were construction in progress and had been invested as capital into Nannan Company. Sanmu Company knew this. Therefore, there was no concealment or fraud by Huangxing Company against Sanmu Company, nor was there a situation where one party took advantage of its superior position or the other party's haste in signing the contracts. The legality of the three Commercial Housing Contracts had been recognized by the civil judgments in [2002] Min Min Chu Zi No. 4 and No. 5, and Sanmu Company should perform them as agreed. The purpose of the Agreement was for Nannan Company to exchange properties for Sanmu Company's legal person shares. The essence of the transaction was that Nannan Company exchanged a certain amount of properties for a certain amount of Sanmu Company's legal person shares, which was an equivalent exchange agreed upon by both parties through consultation, and there was no obvious unfairness.

During the second instance trial, both parties provided evidence that had been examined during the first instance.

To further ascertain the facts of the case and protect the litigation rights of both parties, after the second-instance court trial, this Court again extended the period for submitting evidence for both parties. Within the extended period, Sanmu Company, regarding why it could not provide the original copy of the "Agreement," submitted an explanation concerning the "Agreement" stating, "At that time, after our company and Shenda Company signed and sealed the 'Agreement,' we submitted all original copies of the contract to Nannan Company for signature and sealing. However, after Nannan Company signed and sealed, it only provided photocopies to Sanmu Group and Shenda Company and never returned the original contract, resulting in our company not having the original of the 'Agreement' to this day, and therefore being unable to provide it." The photocopies of three payment vouchers from China Construction Bank totaling RMB 134,870,000 submitted by Sanmu Company had already been examined during the first-instance trial.

Huangxing Company, regarding why the "Agreement" it holds exhibits the fact that "the first two pages and the third page were not printed by the same printing machine, but by different printing machines," submitted an explanation on the burden of proof concerning the tripartite "Agreement" and the "Commercial Housing Contracts." The content of the explanation is: "The 'Agreement' was drafted by Sanmu Company, modified through multi-day negotiations among the three parties, and the final signed text was provided by Sanmu Company. After signing and sealing, each of the three parties kept one copy. We did not pay attention to how many printers Sanmu Company had." Huangxing Company did not provide relevant evidence regarding the signing process of the three "Commercial Housing Contracts." Neither party provided new evidence.

The other facts found by this Court in the second instance are the same as those found by the first-instance court.

Based on Sanmu Company's appeal requests and Huangxing Company's defense, this Court analyzes and determines the focal points of dispute between the parties as follows:

1. Regarding whether Huangxing Company concealed the fact that the properties under the three "Commercial Housing Contracts" had been contributed as investment to Nannan Company, thereby constituting fraud against Sanmu Company.

This Court holds that Sanmu Company acknowledges the fact that it, Shenggongsi, and Nannan Company signed the tripartite "Agreement." The focal point of dispute between the parties on this issue is: Whether the content of Article 5 of the "Agreement," which states "Since the property of Huangxing Building purchased by Sanmu Company is a construction in progress, it has been contributed as investment to Nannan Company as capital," was altered by Huangxing Company. That is, when the three parties signed the "Agreement," whether Huangxing Company concealed from Sanmu Company the fact that the properties under the three "Commercial Housing Contracts" had been contributed as investment to Nannan Company, thereby constituting fraud. The determination of this dispute should be based on Sanmu Company's evidence and Huangxing Company's defense. According to Articles 2, 10, and 34 of the Supreme People's Court's "Several Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings," a party has the responsibility to provide evidence to prove the facts on which its claims are based or to rebut the facts on which the opposing party's claims are based. When a party provides documentary evidence to the People's Court, it shall provide the original and shall actively, comprehensively, and correctly fulfill the obligation of providing evidence within the period for submitting evidence designated by the People's Court. Accordingly, Sanmu Company, as a signatory party to the "Agreement," bears the legal obligation to provide the original of the "Agreement" to support its claim for revocation of the contract. However, Sanmu Company has never been able to provide the original of the "Agreement" from the outset, nor has it been able to provide evidence proving that Huangxing Company's original "Agreement" was not truthfully made and that its content did not represent Sanmu Company's true intention.

Regarding whether the "Explanation" issued by Shenggongsi and provided by Sanmu Company has probative force. Pursuant to Article 70 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Shenggongsi, as a witness aware of the facts of the case, has the obligation to appear in court to testify. As a signatory party to the "Agreement," it should also produce the original "Agreement" to confirm that the photocopy of the "Agreement" held by Sanmu Company is identical to the original. However, Shenggongsi did not appear in court or provide the original "Agreement" regarding the facts to be proved in the dispute between Sanmu Company and Huangxing Company. Therefore, the "Explanation" issued by Shenggongsi has no probative force and is not adopted.

Regarding the probative force of the "Letters of Guarantee" issued by Gaode Company and Huatian Company for Sanmu Company. As found by the first-instance court, the content of the "Agreement" provided by Sanmu Company does not contain a stipulation for Nannan Company to act as guarantor providing a guarantee. Sanmu Company also failed to provide evidence proving that Nannan Company knew of and approved of Gaode Company and Huatian Company providing guarantees for Sanmu Company's performance of the "Agreement." Moreover, the content of the "Letters of Guarantee" cannot prove whether the fact of fraud by Huangxing Company against Sanmu Company existed or was true. Therefore, the "Letters of Guarantee" also cannot be adopted as evidence.

Under the circumstances where the parties disagree on the form and content of the "Agreement," and Sanmu Company, as a signatory party, cannot provide the original "Agreement" or counter-evidence to prove that Huangxing Company's original "Agreement" is untrue, the first-instance court, based on the principle of preponderance of the evidence, determined that the original "Agreement" provided by Huangxing Company could prove that the content of Article 5 of the "Agreement," namely "Since the property of Huangxing Building purchased by Sanmu Company is a construction in progress, it has been contributed as investment to Nannan Company as capital," represented the true intention of the three parties. Adopting this as evidence to find that Sanmu Company knew that Huangxing Company had contributed the properties under the three "Commercial Housing Contracts" as investment to Nannan Company was not improper. Therefore, Sanmu Company's claim that the content of Huangxing Company's original "Agreement" was altered by Huangxing Company and that Huangxing Company concealed this fact from Sanmu Company, constituting fraud, is not supported by this Court.

2. Regarding whether the three "Commercial Housing Contracts" that Sanmu Company requests to revoke are true and lawful.

This Court holds: Sanmu Company acknowledges the fact of signing the three "Commercial Housing Contracts" and acknowledges the authenticity of the official seals and the signature of President Chen Weihui on the three "Commercial Housing Contracts." The focal point of dispute between the parties on this issue is: When the two parties signed the three "Commercial Housing Contracts," whether Huangxing Company concealed the fact that the properties had been transferred as investment to Nannan Company and that Huangxing Company did not have pre-sale qualifications, thereby causing Sanmu Company to make a mistaken expression of intention, constituting fraud against Sanmu Company. Determining this disputed fact first requires ascertaining whether Huangxing Company committed a fraudulent act. According to Article 68 of the Supreme People's Court's "Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (For Trial Implementation)" and Article 54 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, if one party intentionally provides false information to the other party, or intentionally conceals the true situation, inducing the other party to make a mistaken expression of intention, it may be determined as fraud. Only then does the defrauded party have the right to request revocation according to law. In this case, "Huangxing Company, upon approval, as one of the incorporators, contributed as its capital contribution the approved development and construction of the main building of Huangxing Building, floors 1 to 21, the commercial mall floors 3 to 4, and 80 parking spaces on basement floor 1, and on May 26, 2000, incorporated Nannan Company." "The time when the two parties entered into 'Commercial Housing Contract One and Three' was after August 23, 2000; the time when the two parties entered into 'Commercial Housing Contract Two' was after June 15, 2000." The above facts have been found and determined by the effective civil judgments [(2002) Min Chu Zi No. 4 and No. 5], which constitutes an exemption from the burden of proof for Huangxing Company regarding the disputed facts to be proved in this case, and also proves the objective status of the properties under the three "Commercial Housing Contracts" and the circumstances of the parties' signing. Regarding this, whether Huangxing Company could fulfill the obligation to deliver the properties worth RMB 134,870,000, and whether Nannan Company could ensure that the full amount of the proceeds from the sale of the properties received by Huangxing Company was used to purchase the shares of Sanmu Company held by Zhuocheng Company, Gaode Company, and Huatian Company, ultimately achieving the purpose of entering into the three "Commercial Housing Contracts," Sanmu Company was well aware of and should have foreseen. Sanmu Company has never been able to provide evidence proving that, when the two parties entered into the three "Commercial Housing Contracts," Huangxing Company intentionally concealed from Sanmu Company the true status of Huangxing Building.

In this litigation, Sanmu Company has from the outset acknowledged the fact of entering into the three "Commercial Housing Contracts" and the authenticity of its company seal and the signature of its legal representative. The official seal is a statutory instrument for an organization, including state organs, organizations, enterprises, and institutions, to confirm the validity of its external civil activities. The legal representative of a legal person is the person responsible for representing the legal person in exercising its powers according to law or the articles of association of the legal person, and has the authority to represent the legal person in civil activities. All legal consequences arising from actions performed in the course of duty shall be borne by the legal person. Therefore, given that both parties have no objection to the authenticity of Sanmu Company's seal and the signature of its legal representative Chen Weihui on the three "Commercial Housing Contracts," and Sanmu Company cannot prove that the content of the three "Commercial Housing Contracts" was unilaterally filled in by Huangxing Company and that the payment of the RMB 134,870,000 property purchase price and the transfer of equity in accordance with the contracts have been completed, the representations made in the three "Commercial Housing Contracts" shall be deemed to be the result of mutual agreement between the parties. There is no basis to determine that the contracts were entered into due to fraud. The "Pre-sale Application Form for Commercial Housing" submitted by Sanmu Company and completed by Huangxing Company, the "Certificate" issued by Quanzhou Real Estate Administration Bureau, and the "Certificate of House Ownership" No. 2824 also prove that the total pre-sale area of Huangxing Building was 36,039 square meters, while the total area of the properties under the three "Commercial Housing Contracts" was 9,061.34 square meters. Therefore, the first-instance court, based on the "State-owned Land Use Certificate" for Huangxing Building obtained by Huangxing Company and the "Certificate of House Ownership" covering the properties under the three "Commercial Housing Contracts," determined that the properties under the three "Commercial Housing Contracts" had been approved for pre-sale, and that the three "Commercial Housing Contracts" were true, lawful, and valid. This determination has sufficient basis. Sanmu Company's use of the above evidence to deny the true transaction relationship of the property sales between the parties, claiming that Huangxing Company concealed the true status of Huangxing Building's properties and lacked pre-sale qualifications, constituting fraud, and requesting revocation of the three "Commercial Housing Contracts" lacks legal basis.

Regarding Sanmu Company's claim that the prices in the three "Commercial Housing Contracts" were obviously unfair. China's current laws do not clearly define the specific standard for obvious unfairness. The three "Commercial Housing Contracts" in this case explicitly stipulate the main content, including the area, price, payment time and method, and delivery time of the pre-sold properties. The rights and obligations of both parties are complete and genuine, and there is no circumstance where Sanmu Company entered into the contracts due to duress or lack of experience. Moreover, the purchase price of RMB 134,870,000 was already specified in the tripartite "Agreement" signed on June 1, 2000, before the conclusion of the three "Commercial Housing Contracts." Even if the price of the properties under the three "Commercial Housing Contracts" rose compared to the transaction prices of similar properties at that time and place, this falls within the commercial transaction risk that Sanmu Company should have foreseen. Sanmu Company, based on the "Asset Appraisal Report" issued by Fujian Huaxing Accounting Firm, claiming that the property prices stipulated in the three "Commercial Housing Contracts" were obviously unfair and requesting their revocation, also does not meet the statutory requirements for revocation.

3. Regarding whether Sanmu Company's right to apply for investigation of evidence was prejudiced.

This Court holds: Sanmu Company applied to the People's Court for investigation of the properties under the "Commercial Housing Pre-sale Permit" obtained by Huangxing Company. This "Commercial Housing Pre-sale Permit" does not fall within the scope of "evidence that a party cannot collect on its own due to objective reasons" as stipulated in Article 3 of the Supreme People's Court's "Several Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings." In both the first-instance and second-instance proceedings of this case, Sanmu Company also acknowledged the authenticity and legality of the "Commercial Housing Pre-sale Permit" obtained by Huangxing Company. Furthermore, after the second-instance court trial, this Court again extended the period for submitting evidence for Sanmu Company. Therefore, Sanmu Company's litigation rights were not prejudiced.

In summary, the first-instance judgment found that Sanmu Company's request for revocation of the three "Commercial Housing Contracts" did not comply with Article 54 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China. The facts are clear, and the application of the law is correct. Pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

The appeal is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 793,882.86 shall be borne by Fujian Sanmu Group Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Hu Shihao
Judge: Zhang Yafen
Acting Judge: Zhang Yingxin

September 8, 2005

Clerk: Wang Dongying

Senior Judge Hu Shihao: Born in 1964, Master of Laws. Appointed Judge of the Supreme People's Court in 1994.
